strengths: Novel perspective on leveraging function decomposability in distributional optimization with elegant connection to message-passing algorithms
Rigorous mathematical development with multiple derivations (A.3, A.4) providing theoretical depth and robust value function bounds
Comprehensive experimental validation including synthetic benchmarks with exact decompositions and diverse protein design datasets with ablations
Clear algorithmic specification (Algorithm 1) with detailed implementation and promised code availability supporting reproducibility
Practical applicability demonstrated through systematic procedure for deriving decompositions from AlphaFold3 structures
weaknesses: Critical practical limitation inadequately addressed: method requires knowing a good decomposition a priori, but decomposition discovery process is minimally explored; Figure A5 demonstrates high sensitivity to decomposition parameters

Limited baseline comparisons: only naive EDA evaluated; missing comparisons to Factorized Distribution Algorithm, Bayesian optimization methods, and other decomposition-aware approaches mentioned in related work

Mixed empirical results: protein experiments show improvement in 3/4 datasets with TDP-43 showing no difference; improvements are modest (20-40% faster convergence) and diminish with larger sampling budgets (K=1000), questioning practical significance
No theoretical convergence analysis, sample complexity bounds, or characterization of when/why DADO helps; value function bound (Eq. 10) is loose with gap not characterized

Experimental design concerns: per-function hyperparameter sweeps risk unfair comparison; limited protein benchmark (4 main proteins) with one (Gcn4) failing due to invalid decomposition for intrinsically disordered proteins

Scope limitations: method fundamentally depends on decomposition quality but generality to non-protein domains (circuits, materials) is claimed but unvalidated; entire evaluation restricted to discrete amino acids

Algorithm sensitivity to multiple hyperparameters (learning rate η, temperature β, shaping function W, contact threshold t) requiring domain-specific tuning; single gradient step choice justified weakly

strengths: Well-motivated approach addressing a real problem in scientific design where many objectives naturally decompose across design variables
Rigorous theoretical development with principled derivation connecting classical message-passing to distributional optimization, including multiple perspectives and formal proofs

Comprehensive experimental evaluation including systematic synthetic experiments across problem complexities, multiple real protein datasets, proper statistical testing with confidence intervals, and robustness analyses
Consistent improvements across all tested problems compared to appropriate baselines (naive EDA, FDA) in both synthetic and real settings
Strong reproducibility: code available on GitHub, detailed hyperparameters, complete dataset documentation, and experimental setup
Clear presentation with informative figures and well-organized appendices providing thorough technical details
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: primarily applies existing EDA and message-passing frameworks to the decomposition-aware setting; no convergence analysis or optimality guarantees specific to DADO

Strong dependency on known decomposition structure; Figure A6-A7 reveals significant sensitivity to decomposition specification (contact threshold), undermining practical applicability without guidance on determining decomposability in new domains

Modest experimental improvements: overlapping confidence intervals with FDA baseline in several cases; no comparison with other structure-exploiting discrete optimization methods or Bayesian optimization variants

Limited scope of real experiments: only protein property prediction tested; scalability to longer sequences (L > 84) or larger alphabets (D > 21) remains unclear; no demonstration on other scientific design domains
Incomplete analysis of design choices: why synthetic performance gap decreases with L while real improvements persist; limited discussion of failure modes or misspecified decomposition sensitivity
Runtime gains are modest (1-2x) and appear due to sampling efficiency rather than wall-clock improvements; computational complexity analysis is missing

Dense mathematical notation in Sec. 2.1 could be simplified; critical details about decomposition sensitivity buried in appendices; entropy-maximizing variant (A.5) feels disconnected and underdeveloped
All synthetic experiments use similar random junction tree structures; testing on diverse structure types would strengthen claims about generalization
